findings.title: Bitquery on-chain investigation flags suspected $106 million EU crypto theft
findings.summary_md: Bitquery published an on-chain investigation on November 2, 2026 reporting that ZachXBT flagged a suspected theft of more than $106 million from an unidentified European entity across accounts at multiple centralized exchanges, with outflows beginning on Sunday, November 1. The firm traced $108.8 million of the movement and found $61.0 million still on Ethereum.

findings.title: KuCoin: ZachXBT raises suspected EU crypto theft estimate to $133 million
findings.summary_md: KuCoin reported on November 3, 2026 that ZachXBT raised the estimate of the EU theft to more than $133 million after tracing roughly $27 million in additional transactions beyond the original November 1 alert of more than $106 million in stolen USDC and USDT.

findings.title: AMBCrypto: USDC and USDT stolen, ETH swapped, XMR obscured inside a $106M EU hack
findings.summary_md: AMBCrypto reported on November 3, 2026 that, according to ZachXBT, the attacker swapped stolen USDC and USDT into ETH, routed funds through instant exchanges WellWallet and Kyrrex, converted ETH into Monero, and bridged assets across multiple blockchains. ZachXBT stated with high confidence that North Korea's Lazarus Group was not involved.

findings.title: Journal du Coin: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa targeted by $133 million crypto theft per ZachXBT
findings.summary_md: Journal du Coin reported on November 4, 2026 that ZachXBT named Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the institution hit by more than $133 million in crypto withdrawals via Kraken, Ether, and Monero, and that the bank had been exploited for several days without reacting.

findings.title: Cyberattaque.org: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa statement on partner-platform cyberattack
findings.summary_md: Cyberattaque.org published on November 4, 2026 a copy of Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's 17:30 statement saying attackers entered through the platform of a service provider, not through Fortuneo, and reached the bank directly. The bank acknowledged the amounts match the order of magnitude of $133 million without confirming the figure, and said the provider's identity and the exploited platform were not disclosed.
